researcher_notes: CALIBRATION RUN. Single source file '1688618048.pdf' (6pp) is itself a mini-catalog documenting THREE reach-truck payload variants of the VNR family back-to-back: VNR14 (pp.1-2, NOT in DB -- new), VNR16 (pp.3-4, already in DB), VNR20 (pp.5-6, already in DB). All three share the same chassis architecture, options list, and footnote text almost verbatim ('*Customizable 3D SLAM navigation; come with triplex mast option with lifting height 5755mm, 7255mm, 8555mm...'), confirming this is a genuine payload-variant family, not three unrelated products. This calibration run only had time to fully extract VNR14 (new); VNR16/VNR20 were cross-checked against the existing DB rows and TWO conflicts were found on each (lifting_height, min_aisle_width) -- flagged below, not overwritten. Text extraction quality note: this vendor's PDF interleaves the metric and imperial figures character-by-character in a way that pdfplumber's column-merge garbles badly for the 'Vehicle Dimensions (l1/b1/h1)' rows specifically (e.g. 'Mast Retracts (2 645 .18 37 x3x 91 .66 9x3 155 4x .33 3i9 n)20mm') -- these vehicle_length/width/height figures were deliberately left UNFILLED rather than guessed from the garbled text; every other spec table row on these pages extracted cleanly and was used with confidence. Also note: DS Automotion, Toyota and this VisionNav sheet all independently confirmed the same variant-completion pattern this run (a single manufacturer file covering several payload-class siblings of one chassis) -- worth building an explicit checklist item for the full batch: 'does this file contain more than one model number in its own text/table headers?'  ---  ADDENDUM (same-day continuation batch, full-New/-folder run): 7 more individual VisionNav product datasheets processed (1688464515.pdf=VNSL14, 1688613405.pdf=VNP15, 1775592252.pdf=VNKQ20, 1775593635.pdf=VNE40, 1775596770.pdf=VNQ50, 1775597593.pdf=VNK15, 1785316235.pdf+dup-2.pdf=VNE20). ALL SEVEN already exist in the DB as base models with literally every field NULL ('last_updated: unknown') -- pure enrichment, no new products, no variant completion needed (each already has its own base_model row). Existing DB product_type was respected as-is and NOT re-derived from the datasheet content even where it looked debatable (see VNKQ20 note in that product's own notes field). For SCORING-level max_speed, this batch consistently used the LOADED (lower, more conservative) figure from the 'Loaded/Empty' pairs printed in each motion-performance table, whereas the VNR14 entry above (calibration run) had used the marketing headline figure instead -- flagging this inconsistency between the two sub-batches rather than silently harmonizing it; both are grounded in real printed numbers, just a different convention pick. Three deferred full-line VisionNav catalogs (1657089341.pdf EN 18pp, 1685356775.pdf EN 14pp, 1728979799.pdf ES 16pp) were explicitly NOT opened for extraction this run (all listed products already covered by individual datasheets in the DB; catalogs are marketing/company overview, low marginal value for the time cost) -- left in New/, see coverage report.  ---  ADDENDUM (final-8-files run, same calendar day): '1685356775.pdf' turned out NOT to be a generic full-line catalog after all -- it is a dedicated 14-page single-product deck for the VNST20 'All In One Pallet Jack' (model number only visible on the p.1 cover image as large stylized text, not extractable as text -- resolved by rendering p.1 as an image). This RESOLVES the earlier open question (flagged in agent memory) about an 'unassigned 2000kg payload spec block' seen in this file -- it belongs to VisionNav VNST20, an EXISTING DB product, and its 2000kg payload / 1.8 m/s empty-load speed both match the already-stored DB values exactly (confirmed, not new). New enrichment fields added below. '1657089341.pdf' (18pp EN) and '1728979799.pdf' (16pp ES) were both opened and are genuine multi-product full-line catalogs (confirmed via cover-page images -- 'Products Catalog / Full Range of Autonomous Industrial Vehicles' resp. its Spanish equivalent), NOT single-product decks like 1685356775.pdf turned out to be. Text extraction quality on BOTH is clean (unlike prior VisionNav files that needed table-extraction or image fallback), so a full read was practical this run. '1728979799.pdf' (Spanish) was found to be almost entirely CONFIRMATORY of already-DB-covered products (ST/SL/P/E/R/Q series = VNST20, VNSL14, VNP15/20/30, VNR14/16/20, VNE20/30/35/40, VNQ50, all already in the DB with fields substantially filled from earlier individual-datasheet sessions) -- given the low marginal enrichment value and this run's remaining time budget, it was NOT deep-extracted field-by-field; only spot-checked for genuinely new content (none found beyond what English sources already cover). '1657089341.pdf' (English), by contrast, contains THREE genuinely new model families never seen in any prior VisionNav file or DB row: T Series (Pallet Jack AGV, VNT20), L Series (Pallet Stacker Forklift AGV, VNL14/VNL16), and two new Q-series tow-tractor payload classes (VNQ40/VNQ60, distinct from the already-DB VNQ50) -- these WERE fully extracted this run, see new product entries below. The English catalog's R-series pages (VNR14/VNR16/VNR25) were deliberately NOT used to create or update product rows, despite containing real spec tables: they introduce THIRD AND FOURTH sub-variant suffixes (-01 manual-seated-retractable, -07 manual-handheld, -07 manual-seated-tiller, -07 standing-tiller-only-for-VNR25) for model codes that already have open conflicts flagged from the calibration run (VNR16/VNR20 lifting_height + min_aisle_width conflicts) -- and the catalog's own page 13 vs page 15 print TWO DIFFERENT spec sets both labelled 'VNR16(V)-07' (Manual Handheld: 4500kg body weight, 6300mm lift height vs Manual Seated: 3910kg body weight, 7000mm lift height) which is an internal naming collision in the vendor's own document, not just a DB-vs-datasheet conflict. Adding more same-numbered R-series rows right now risks compounding an already-flagged reconciliation problem rather than resolving it -- flagged in the coverage report as a dedicated R-series reconciliation task for the Tech Lead (needs a decision on whether operation-type sub-variants, e.g. '-07 Handheld' vs '-07 Seated', should become separate Product rows with disambiguating names, and how that interacts with the existing VNR16/VNR20 conflict flags). Raw R-series figures from this catalog are recorded in researcher_notes only, not written to any field, so nothing is lost if a later session picks this up.
